analysis.investment_thesis: Gillette India is a textbook Munger-quality business — ROCE of 58.78%, zero debt, 63% gross margins, and 100%+ FCF conversion — backed by the most dominant grooming brand on earth. However, at 48x earnings for a ~10% revenue grower, the price already reflects perfection and leaves a Munger-style investor with insufficient margin of safety to initiate aggressively.
key_strengths: ROCE 58.78% with literally zero debt — a rare, capital-light compounder that earns extraordinary returns without leverage
FCF/Net Income of 107% (INR 442 Cr / INR 412 Cr) — earnings quality is pristine, no accounting games
63% gross margins underpin durable pricing power from the Gillette/P&G global brand franchise — India's #1 razor brand by far
key_risks: 48x P/E for a 9.4% revenue CAGR grower is pricing in a flawless future — any margin compression or growth miss destroys the thesis
India's mass market is highly price-sensitive; Guard (low-ASP razor) limits premiumization and constrains blended revenue growth to single digits
75% promoter (P&G) means minority investors are along for the ride — capital allocation decisions (INR 440 Cr financing outflow in FY24, mostly dividends up to parent) are not in their hands
red_flags: P/E of 48.45x on 9-10% growth implies a very long payback period — no margin of safety for the intelligent investor
Revenue growth decelerating at the margin (2,477→2,633 Cr, ~6.3% in FY24) while the multiple stays elevated
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Gillette India passes every quality test I apply: ROCE of 58.78% obliterates my 20% threshold, gross margins of 63% scream real pricing power, and the balance sheet carries zero rupee of debt with INR 473 Cr in cash. The business has converted over 100% of net income to free cash flow for four consecutive years — that is the hallmark of a business that doesn't need to fabricate earnings. P&G's global R&D pipeline continuously refreshes the product portfolio (GilletteLabs, Fusion5, SkinGuard) while the distribution moat through kirana stores and modern trade is essentially unreplicable. This is the kind of business I would own forever if the price were right.

The price, however, is the problem. At 48x earnings and 28x EV/EBITDA, Mr. Market is already pricing in 15%+ earnings growth indefinitely. Actual revenue has grown at 9.4% CAGR, and the last year showed only 6.3%. India's grooming market has genuine underpenetration upside, but price-sensitive consumers anchor the bottom of the pyramid on the INR 10 Guard razor — premiumization is gradual. I would not sell this business if I owned it, but deploying fresh capital at 48x for a ~10% grower violates my requirement for an adequate margin of safety. Wait for a meaningful correction — closer to 30-35x — before adding aggressively.
